subject: Endeavor POC — model tradeoffs, prompt sets, and mutual plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@endeavor.ai>, Priya Raman <priya@endeavor.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial post-demo recap + quick read on model fit

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate the practical examples you showed for the ticket summarization flow. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard (reconfirming constraints)
- Avg document length: 1.2k tokens, but 15% of docs reach 6k tokens (legal attachments).
- SLO: 95th percentile generation latency < 400ms for the 512-token tail; budget target $0.6 / 1k output tokens.
- Privacy: logs stored for 30 days, production data cannot leave your EU region when using private deployment.

Preliminary model shortlist (for evaluation):
1) Open-quant-70B (8-bit) — high-quality instruction-following, expected latency ~450–550ms on reserved A100-style capacity; best for accuracy-sensitive outputs.
2) LlamaX-33B-q4 — lower latency (~250–350ms), much cheaper per-token with modest quality drop on long-context summarization.
3) Redwood-compat-13B — fast (<200ms), good for extractive/rerank tasks and useful as a safety/fallback route.

What we’ll validate in the next round:
- Prompt set priming: we’ll run the demo prompts you used plus a representative 200-case prompt set (attached prompt_set_v1.txt).
- Benchmarks: token-level latency and ROUGE/ROUGE-L + answer-exactness checks for the summarization task. Summary CSV attached (endeavor_poc_benchmark_summary.csv) will be updated after we run the full suite.
- Regression risk: we’ll flag any >3% drop in answer-exactness vs. the baseline you provided.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Alex/Priya: please confirm the 200-case prompt set is representative or drop pointers to additional edge cases by Tue EOD PST.
- We’ll schedule a 45-min technical run (bench + prompt refinement) next Wed — does 11am PT work?
- I’ll loop in engineering (Marissa) and sales ops (Karthik) for pricing and mutual action plan.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompts), benchmark_summary stub CSV.

Thanks — jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@endeavor.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya@endeavor.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial post-demo recap + quick read on model fit

Thanks Jasmine — this is great. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the benchmark run:

- For the 15% docs at 6k tokens: do you recommend truncation with extractive highlights before generation, or moving to a longer-context model for those cases? Latency impact is our main concern.
- On the 3% regression threshold: can you define "answer-exactness" metric? Is that strict string match or normalized semantic match?

11am PT next Wed works for us. We’ll also invite our infra lead (Sam Park) on the call — he may ask about VPC/private deployment options if the 70B variant looks necessary.

Also, curious on cost delta: how much cheaper is the LlamaX-33B-q4 vs Open-quant-70B in your experience for mixed workloads? Even a ballpark per-1k-token ratio helps justify tradeoffs to procurement.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Endeavor Analytics

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Initial post-demo recap + quick read on model fit (internal)

Looping you both so we can prep the run and pricing. Notes for the bench run and what I want from engineering: 

Marissa — bench plan
- Run prompt_set_v1.txt against the three candidates (Open-quant-70B-8bit, LlamaX-33B-q4, Redwood-compat-13B) on 512 and 2048 truncation settings; include two long-doc strategies: (A) naive truncation at 2048, (B) extractive prefilter + 2048.
- Collect: token latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), peak GPU memory, and exactness scores. For exactness use normalized token-level F1 + a semantic-similarity threshold (cosine on USE embeddings) with human spot-check on 50 cases.
- Add KV-cache warmup runs to show steady-state vs cold-start.

Karthik — pricing / next steps
- Prepare two pricing scenarios for the POC: (1) Dedicated capacity with reserved A100s for the 70B path, (2) Hosted API with autoscaling for the 33B fallback. Include a 3-month pilot price + uplift for EU-region private deployment.
- We’ll propose a mutual action plan (MAP). I attached a stub (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) with milestones (bench complete, data ingestion dry-run, security review, POC kickoff).

Quick answers to Alex’s questions inline so you’re aligned when we push final doc: 
- Long docs: if you need sub-400ms p95 for 512 tokens, the 70B is unlikely to meet that without higher-cost hardware. A hybrid strategy (Redwood-compat-13B for initial extractive pass + 70B only for complex cases) is likely best.
- "Answer-exactness": propose combined metric — normalized token-F1 + human spot-check for semantic correctness. We’ll treat >3% drop on token-F1 as a red flag and escalate.
- Cost delta: preliminary ballpark: LlamaX-33B-q4 ~35–45% of the per-token cost of Open-quant-70B on our hosted stacks; we’ll quantify in the pricing doc.

I’ll produce the full benchmark runbook and send to Alex/Priya after we collect the first run.

Thanks — jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@endeavor.ai>, Priya Raman <priya@endeavor.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Endeavor POC — refined shortlist, bench timing, and MAP

Alex/Priya — following the internal bench planning, here’s a refined recommendation and concrete asks so we can get the POC scoped: 

Refined model shortlist & rationale
- Option A (Accuracy-first): Open-quant-70B-8bit
  - Rationale: best pass at abstractive, long-context coherence for legal/edge cases. Higher latency and cost; recommended only if accuracy gains on the 200-case set exceed 6% vs 33B on normalized token-F1.
- Option B (Balanced): LlamaX-33B-q4 + Redwood-compat-13B fallback
  - Rationale: 33B is the best balance for ticket summarization at your target latency and cost; the 13B model covers quick reranking/extractive steps cheaply. Likely meets cost target in hosted mode with burst capacity.
- Option C (Latency-first): Redwood-compat-13B + extractive preprocessing
  - Rationale: Lowest latency and cost; recommend if p95 for 512 tokens must be <300ms. Less accurate on abstractive items.

Planned deliverables for the bench run (we'll deliver the artifacts within 48 hours of the run):
- Updated benchmark CSV with p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1k-token column (endeavor_poc_benchmark_summary.csv).
- Prompt set results snapshot (prompt_set_v1.txt produced per-model outputs).
- A short regression note if any model shows >3% token-F1 drop vs baseline and a human-checked sample.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- Tue EOD: Alex confirms edge-case prompts and signs off on bench scope.
- Wed 11am PT: Technical bench run + prompt tuning call (we’ll run live and deliver artifacts).
- Following week: security questionnaire + private deployment scoping if we choose Option A.

Next asks
- Please confirm the 200-case prompt set (I’ll accept feedback inline on the Drive link) and if Sam Park should be added to the bench call.
- If Option A looks required after the first run, we’ll prepare an EU-region private deployment price sheet (Karthik will send).

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.txt, endeavor_poc_benchmark_summary.csv (stub; will be updated), mutual_action_plan.xlsx

If that all looks good I’ll set the Wed invite and share the Drive folder with the run artifacts.

Best — jasmine
